topic: Important Stadiums in India and the World (Static GK)
description: A comprehensive study guide covering major sports stadiums across India and the globe, their locations, and associated sports, optimized for the static general knowledge section of competitive exams.

sections.title: Major Cricket Stadiums of India
sections.description: Prominent cricket grounds in India along with their geographical locations and historical significance.

geographical_data.key_characteristics: It is the largest cricket stadium in the world by seating capacity. It was formerly known as the Motera Stadium.
Often referred to as the 'Mecca of Indian Cricket', it is the oldest and second-largest cricket stadium in India.
It serves as the headquarters of the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) and hosted the iconic 2011 ICC Cricket World Cup final.
Locally known as the Chepauk Stadium, it is one of the oldest continuously used cricket grounds in India.
A major international cricket stadium previously known as the Feroz Shah Kotla Stadium.

sections.title: Other Important Sports Stadiums in India
sections.description: Famous sports complexes in India dedicated to sports other than cricket, such as football, hockey, and athletics.

key_associations.item: Salt Lake Stadium (Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan)
key_associations.extra_info: It is the largest football stadium in India by seating capacity and one of the largest in the world.

sections.title: Famous Stadiums of the World
sections.description: Historically significant and iconic sports grounds at the international level.

geographical_data.key_characteristics: Widely known as the 'Home of Cricket', it is owned by the Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC).
It is the second-largest cricket stadium in the world and the largest stadium in the Southern Hemisphere.
The largest football stadium in the United Kingdom and the home ground of the England national football team.
One of the most iconic football stadiums globally, it has hosted two FIFA World Cup finals (1950 and 2014).
Famous for hosting the French Open, which is the only Grand Slam tennis tournament played on clay courts.

sections.title: Important Facts and Superlatives
sections.description: Crucial one-liner facts and extremes related to stadiums frequently asked in competitive exams.

important_facts.fact: The Rungrado 1st of May Stadium, located in Pyongyang, North Korea, is the largest stadium in the world by overall seating capacity.
The Himachal Pradesh Cricket Association (HPCA) Stadium in Dharamshala is recognized as one of the highest altitude international cricket stadiums in the world.
The Wimbledon tennis tournament is played on grass courts at the All England Lawn Tennis and Croquet Club in London, making it the oldest tennis tournament in the world.
Green Park Stadium is a prominent international cricket stadium uniquely situated on the banks of the river Ganga in Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh.
Arthur Ashe Stadium in New York, USA, is the largest tennis stadium in the world by capacity and serves as the main venue for the US Open.
